objects.description: Function pointer type for asynchronous message reporting. The callback receives a user context pointer, an integer code, and a float value. Often used to deliver status/progress/errors from decoders to client code. Details like code semantics are not documented here.

Function pointer type for audio/video synchronization queries. The callback takes a user context pointer and returns a long value (e.g., a timestamp or clock in milliseconds). Exact units/semantics are not specified in this header.

Abstract interface for a media decoder. Provides lifecycle control (Start/Pause/Stop), duration and current position queries, seeking, and a way to set a message callback. As a pure virtual class, it cannot be instantiated directly; concrete subclasses must implement all methods. Ownership/lifetime of the callback context is managed by the caller; threading behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: Decoder::Start
functions.description: Starts the decoding/playback process for a concrete Decoder implementation. Pure virtual interface method; behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
No arguments; thread-safety or call ordering (e.g., requiring prior initialization) is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: Decoder::Pause
functions.description: Pauses the decoding/playback process for a concrete Decoder implementation. Pure virtual interface method; behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
Call ordering and thread-safety guarantees are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: Decoder::Stop
functions.description: Stops the decoding/playback process for a concrete Decoder implementation. Pure virtual interface method; behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
Whether Stop can be called multiple times and its effect on subsequent Start calls is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: Decoder::GetDuration
functions.description: Returns the total media duration as a float for a concrete Decoder implementation. Pure virtual; unit is not explicitly documented.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
Return unit (e.g., seconds) is not specified; typical decoders use seconds (inferred).

functions.name: Decoder::SeekToPosition
functions.description: Seeks the decoder to the specified playback position. Pure virtual; exact behavior and units are implementation-defined. Typically position represents seconds (inferred).
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
Argument position is a float. Valid range, clamping/rounding behavior, and units are not specified in this header (unknown; commonly 0..GetDuration in seconds, inferred).

functions.name: Decoder::GetCurrentPosition
functions.description: Returns the current playback position for the decoder as a float. Pure virtual; unit is not explicitly documented.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
Return unit is not specified; typically seconds (inferred).

functions.name: Decoder::SetMessageCallback
functions.signature: virtual void Decoder::SetMessageCallback(void* context, MessageCallback callback) = 0;
functions.description: Registers a message callback for decoder events. MessageCallback is typedef'ed as void (*)(void*, int, float). The decoder may invoke the callback with the provided context, an integer code, and a float value. Pure virtual; exact event semantics are implementation-defined.
requirements: Must be called on a concrete subclass implementing Decoder.
callback must be a function pointer compatible with: void (*)(void*, int, float).
context is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; its meaning/lifetime management is caller-defined.
Whether callback can be null to clear callbacks is not specified (unknown).
Thread-safety and the thread on which the callback is invoked are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: ThreadSafeQueue::ThreadSafeQueue
functions.description: Default constructor for a thread-safe queue wrapper around std::queue<T>. Initializes an empty queue with an internal mutex and condition variable.
requirements: Type T must be a valid template argument for std::queue<T>.
No additional initialization required.

functions.name: ThreadSafeQueue::ThreadSafeQueue
functions.description: Copy-constructs a ThreadSafeQueue by taking a lock on the source and copying its underlying queue state.
requirements: Type T must be copy-constructible to allow copying of std::queue<T>.
The constructor acquires other.m_mutex; other must remain valid for the duration of the copy.

functions.name: ThreadSafeQueue::Push
functions.description: Pushes a new element into the queue in a mutex-protected manner and notifies one waiting thread via the condition variable (note: this class does not provide a waiting pop).
requirements: Type T must be copyable or movable (std::queue<T>::push requires copy/move).
new_value is pushed by value; ownership semantics are those of T.
Safe to call concurrently with other Push/Pop calls; internal mutex protects the queue.

functions.name: ThreadSafeQueue::Pop
functions.description: Pops and returns the front element under lock. If the queue is empty, returns nullptr instead of an element. Does not block or wait on the condition variable.
requirements: Type T must be compatible with nullptr (e.g., a pointer type), because the function returns nullptr when the queue is empty; using a non-pointer T will not compile or will misbehave.
Caller must handle a potential nullptr return indicating the queue was empty.
Returned element is removed from the queue; ownership/lifetime semantics depend on T.

functions.name: ThreadSafeQueue::Empty
functions.description: Returns whether the underlying queue is empty. Note: implementation does not acquire the mutex, so the result can race with concurrent Push/Pop operations.
requirements: Because this method does not lock, callers must avoid relying on it for synchronization-sensitive decisions under concurrency, or provide external synchronization.
Return value is a snapshot and may be stale immediately in multi-threaded contexts.

functions.name: ThreadSafeQueue::Size
functions.description: Returns the number of elements currently in the queue while holding the internal mutex.
requirements: No special requirements; provides a snapshot size under the lock.
Return type is int; very large queues may overflow int (inferred).
